**1. Asset & Parties Snapshot** | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | **Biotech (US‑based)** | Pre‑revenue, single Phase 3 oncology asset; potential FDA accelerated‑approval pathway (e.g., breakthrough therapy). | | **Pharma (EU‑based)** | Established commercial platform in EU/UK; strong regulatory & sales network. | | **Deal Structure** | • Upfront fee + development milestones
• Tiered royalty on net sales
• Territorial split: US rights to Biotech, EU/UK rights to Pharma | --- ## 2. Valuation Framework – rNPV ### 2.1 Core Assumptions (illustrative) | Parameter | Value | Rationale | |-----------|-------|-----------| | **Probability of Phase 3 success** | 0.55 | Historical oncology P‑3 success ~55% | | **Time to FDA approval** | 18 mo after P‑3 start | Accelerated pathway reduces time | | **Time to EMA approval** | 24 mo after FDA filing (parallel) | EU/UK approvals often follow FDA | | **Launch price (US)** | $1,200 per patient/year | Comparable oncology drugs | | **Market size (US)** | 30,000 patients in first year | Based on disease incidence & eligibility | | **Growth rate** | 10 % CAGR for 5 yr | Conservative growth assumption | | **Discount rate** | 12 % (adjusted for biotech risk) | Reflects high‑risk nature | | **Tax rate** | 21 % (US), 15 % (EU) | Effective corporate tax rates | ### 2.2 Cash‑Flow Model 1. **Revenue Forecast** *Net sales* = Patients × Price × (1 – Discount/Promotions). Apply royalty % to determine cash flow to each party. 2. **Cost Structure** - Clinical development costs (Phase 3, regulatory filings) - Commercialization & marketing expenses (Pharma in EU/UK; Biotech in US) 3. **Net Cash Flow** = Revenue – Costs – Taxes 4. **NPV Calculation** \[ NPV = \sum_{t=1}^{T} \frac{CF_t}{(1+r)^t} \] where \(r\) is the discount rate. 5. **Risk Adjustment** Multiply NPV by probability of success (0.55). Resulting *risk‑adjusted NPV* (rNPV) represents the expected value to each party under a baseline scenario. ### 2.3 Scenario Analysis | Scenario | P‑3 Success | FDA Approval | EMA Approval | rNPV (US) | rNPV (EU/UK) | |----------|-------------|--------------|--------------|-----------|--------------| | Base | 55 % | 18 mo | 24 mo | $1.2 B | $0.9 B | | Optimistic | 70 % | 12 mo | 18 mo | $1.8 B | $1.4 B | | Pessimistic | 40 % | 30 mo | 36 mo | $0.7 B | $0.5 B | *Use these to benchmark upfront/milestone levels.* --- ## 3. Deal Structure – Cash‑Flow & Risk Allocation ### 3.1 Upfront Payment - **Purpose**: Immediate capital for Biotech; signals Pharma’s commitment. - **Typical Range**: 10–20 % of projected rNPV (US side). *Example*: $120 M upfront if US rNPV = $600 M. ### 3.2 Development Milestones | Milestone | Trigger | Payment | Rationale | |-----------|---------|---------|-----------| | **Phase 3 start** | Signed protocol & IND approval | $30 M | Covers early P‑3 costs | | **Interim analysis (≥70 % enrollment)** | Data review meeting | $20 M | Aligns with risk of attrition | | **FDA NDA filing** | Submission date | $25 M | Reflects regulatory effort | | **FDA approval** | 30‑day FDA decision | $40 M | Captures accelerated pathway benefit | | **EMA submission** | Post‑FDA filing | $15 M | Covers EU regulatory costs | | **EMA approval** | Decision within 90 days | $20 M | Aligns with EU launch | ### 3.3 Commercialization Milestones | Milestone | Trigger | Payment | Rationale | |-----------|---------|---------|-----------| | **First‑year US sales ≥$200 M** | Net sales threshold | $30 M | Incentivizes early commercial success | | **Cumulative EU/UK sales ≥$150 M** | Net sales threshold | $20 M | Reflects Pharma’s market reach | | **Global sales ≥$500 M** | Cumulative worldwide | $25 M | Aligns long‑term upside | ### 3.4 Tiered Royalty - **US (Biotech)** - 12 % on first $200 M net sales - 10 % on $200–$500 M - 8 % beyond $500 M - **EU/UK (Pharma)** - 9 % on first €150 M net sales - 7 % on €150–€400 M - 5 % thereafter *Royalty caps can be negotiated to protect each party’s upside.* ### 3.5 Territorial Rights - **US**: Biotech retains exclusive commercialization rights; Pharma may license to third‑party distributors if needed. - **EU/UK**: Pharma holds exclusivity; Biotech receives a royalty on sales. *This split mitigates regulatory risk (FDA vs EMA) and leverages each party’s strengths.* --- ## 4. Risk‑Sharing Framework | Risk Category | Exposure | Mitigation / Allocation | |---------------|----------|------------------------| | **Clinical Development** | Phase 3 attrition, safety signals | Milestone payments tied to enrollment & interim data; Biotech bears early development costs | | **Regulatory Approval** | FDA/EMA delays or denials | Separate regulatory milestones; “Regulatory risk share” clause: if approval fails, milestone payments are reduced proportionally | | **Commercialization** | Market uptake, pricing pressure | Tiered royalties provide upside; first‑year sales milestone protects against weak launch | | **IP & Exclusivity** | Patent infringement, data exclusivity lapses | Biotech retains ownership of core IP; Pharma obtains license for EU/UK with 5‑yr exclusivity; cross‑licensing for companion diagnostics | | **Currency & Tax** | USD/EUR fluctuations, transfer pricing | Use hedging instruments; structure payments in local currencies; apply tax‑efficient entities (e.g., CFC rules) | | **Post‑Market Obligations** | Safety reporting, risk management plans | Joint responsibility; cost sharing defined in the agreement | --- ## 5. Financial Structure – Deal Economics ### 5.1 Expected Cash Flows to Each Party | Component | Biotech (US) | Pharma (EU/UK) | |-----------|--------------|----------------| | Upfront | $120 M | $0 | | Development Milestones | $140 M | $70 M | | Commercialization Milestones | $85 M | $55 M | | Royalty Income (5‑yr avg.) | $180 M | $110 M | | **Total Expected Cash** | **$525 M** | **$235 M** | *These figures are illustrative; actual numbers will be derived from the rNPV model.* ### 5.2 Net Present Value of Deal - **Biotech NPV** = Upfront + PV(milestones) + PV(royalties) – Development costs - **Pharma NPV** = PV(milestones) + PV(royalties) – Marketing & distribution costs *Both parties should compare the deal NPV to an alternative (e.g., Biotech’s standalone launch or Pharma’s independent acquisition).* ### 5.3 Sensitivity Analysis | Variable | Impact on Biotech NPV | Impact on Pharma NPV | |----------|-----------------------|----------------------| | FDA approval time (+6 mo) | –$30 M | –$15 M | | First‑year sales drop 20 % | –$25 M | –$10 M | | Royalty rate increase 2 pp | +$15 M | +$8 M | *Use these to negotiate milestone thresholds and royalty tiers.* --- ## 6. Milestone Calibration – Practical Steps 1. **Benchmark against comparable deals** (e.g., oncology accelerated‑approval collaborations). 2. **Align milestones with internal project timelines** (clinical, regulatory, commercial). 3. **Incorporate probability of success at each trigger**; higher risk stages receive larger milestone payments. 4. **Include “soft” milestones** (e.g., data lock, IND renewal) to keep the partnership on track. 5. **Set clear performance metrics** for commercialization milestones (sales thresholds, market share). --- ## 7. IP & Regulatory Exposure Across Jurisdictions | Issue | US | EU/UK | |-------|----|-------| | **Patent Protection** | 20‑year term from filing; data exclusivity 5 yr | 20‑year term; data exclusivity 8 yr (EU) | | **Orphan Drug Status** | Potential 7‑yr exclusivity | Potential 10‑yr exclusivity | | **Regulatory Exclusivities** | FDA 5 yr for new molecular entity | EMA 3 yr for first‑in‑class; 2 yr for orphan | | **Companion Diagnostics** | Must be co‑approved with drug | Same requirement; data sharing agreements needed | *Ensure the license agreement covers all IP rights, including any required companion diagnostic patents.* --- ## 8. Key Takeaways & Recommendations 1. **Use rNPV as the core valuation engine** – it captures probability of success and time‑value of money. 2. **Structure milestones to mirror risk progression** – early development costs borne by Biotech; regulatory approvals trigger larger payments. 3. **Tiered royalties provide upside while protecting each party’s investment** – calibrate tiers based on realistic sales forecasts. 4. **Territorial split aligns with each party’s strengths and reduces regulatory friction** – US for Biotech, EU/UK for Pharma. 5. **Incorporate explicit risk‑sharing clauses** (regulatory failure, commercial underperformance) to keep the partnership balanced. 6. **Perform sensitivity analysis on key variables** (approval timing, sales volume, royalty rates) before finalizing terms. 7. **Secure robust IP and exclusivity provisions** across both jurisdictions to safeguard future revenues. By following this structured approach, both parties can align incentives, manage risk effectively, and maximize the commercial potential of the oncology asset.
